title: PNP identifies 70 social media posts encouraging protests, violence
summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Friday said it has identified around 70 social media posts allegedly encouraging people to participate in protests and engage in violence.

blocks.text: The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Friday said it has identified around 70 social media posts allegedly encouraging people to participate in protests and engage in violence.
At a press briefing, PNP spokesperson Police Brigadier General Allen Rae Co said the PNP Anti-Cybercrime Group is working to identify the individuals or groups behind the posts.
“Marami po, marami ang na-ano natin na, several. Siguro nasa mga 70, more or less, 70,” Co said.
(There were several. Maybe more or less 70.)

Among the posts monitored by authorities were messages urging people to take to the streets, join demonstrations, oust certain government officials, and resort to violence over alleged government’s wrongdoing.
Co said the PNP is still validating the identities of those behind the posts.
According to him, authorities have noticed similarities in some of the messages, including the use of identical punctuation marks and spacing.
“It could have come from a single source na marami pong naglalabas (and many people posted them),” he said.
Co said the PNP is examining possible violations of Philippine laws in connection with the posts.
During the ASEAN Summit 2026, protesters expressed opposition to the Pax Silica initiative as well as the visit of United States President Donald Trump to the Philippines. —NB, GMA News
